action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. ## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 3f0286c7-f16f-4875-8271-99d2c7eaf7d9
Personal Orchestrator — one front door to your domain services (career, applications,
documents, tasks, mail, contacts).

How to work:
1. Discover with list_capabilities (each has a risk class + confirm policy); act with
   call_capability(capability_id, input, confirm?). read/draft run immediately; update
   may require confirmation; external (send/delete/pay) ALWAYS requires confirm:true.
2. On status "approval_required", show the user exactly what will happen, then re-call
   with confirm:true. For multi-step goals use preview_action_plan → execute_approved_plan.
3. call_service_tool is a low-level bypass; prefer call_capability for normal use.

Intent → action — match the user's INTENT before touching a tool:
- "write / formulate / draft me an email", "how would I reply?" → just WRITE THE TEXT in
  the chat. Do NOT call any mail tool. ("Entwurf"/"draft" alone can mean a text draft.)
- "put it in my mailbox / in Proton / as a draft", "prepare the mail", "don't send, just
  draft" → mail.append_draft (a real Proton draft you review/send on your phone).
- "send it / schick ab / verschick das" → mail.send_draft (external, irreversible). First
  show recipient, subject, body and attachments and get explicit confirmation.
- When unsure whether the user wants just text or a real mailbox draft, default to TEXT in
  the chat and ask. Never send as a side effect of "write".

Source of truth:
- For real CVs, cover letters, applications and career data, use the content capabilities
  (career.* / application.* / cv.generate / cl.generate) — never hand-write a CV/letter or
  invent a PDF. Attach a generated PDF by passing its downloadUrl to mail.append_draft (it
  is fetched and attached as the real file; never paste the link into the body).
- Choose the sender with mail.list_identities + the "from" field when the user names an account.

If a tool fails: report the real error and stop. Do NOT work around the architecture — no
self-made PDFs, no alternative mail paths, no claiming success when nothing happened.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## nexus-mac-mini-m4-prod
This is the nexus instance "mac-mini-m4-prod" (example.com), running build 3093801 across 1 machine. Everything you do here lands on THIS cluster — if several nexus servers are connected, check this name before acting. Start with list_capabilities; org.list tells you which workspaces exist, and apps and stores must name the one they live in. A value that SEVERAL apps need belongs on their group (deploy.group_env) — stored once and injected into every member — not copied into each app with deploy.set_env; that copy is what makes it impossible to rotate later.

import json

from collections import Counter

import pandas as pd

XLSX = sys.argv[1]
OUT = sys.argv[2]

PATTERNS = {
    "Mercedes": r"mercedes|\bmerc\b|\bmercs\b|\bbenz\b|\bmb\b|\bamg\b|\b[aceGgs][- ]?class\b|\bcla\b|\bgl[abcse]\b|\beq[abces]\b|\beqs?\d|maybach|\bw21[34]\b",

    "Tesla": r"\btesla|model [s3xy]\b|\bmodel3\b|\bmodely\b|supercharg|\bfsd\b|full self[- ]driving|autopilot|cybertruck",
    "Lexus": r"\blexus|\b(es|ls|gs|is|rx|nx)\s?\d{3}h?\b",
    "Genesis": r"\bgenesis|\bg[789]0\b|\bgv[678]0\b",
    "Cadillac": r"cadillac|lyriq|celestiq|\bct[456]\b|\bescalade|super ?cruise",
    "Porsche": r"porsche|taycan|panamera|macan|cayenne|\b911\b",
    "VW": r"\bvw\b|volkswagen|\bgolf\b|\bpassat\b|\bid\.?\s?[347]\b|\barteon\b|\btouareg\b",
    "Volvo": r"volvo|\bxc[469]0\b|\b[sv][69]0\b",
    "Polestar": r"polestar",
    "Lucid": r"\blucid\b|\bair\b(?= (?:pure|touring|grand))",
    "Rivian": r"rivian|\br1[st]\b",
    "Hyundai/Kia": r"hyundai|\bkia\b|ioniq|\bev[369]\b|\bsonata\b|\bstinger\b|telluride",
    "Toyota/Honda": r"toyota|\bhonda\b|\bcamry\b|\bprius\b|\baccord\b|\bcivic\b|\bcr-?v\b|\brav-?4\b",
    "Nissan": r"nissan|\bleaf\b|\bariya\b",
    "Ford/GM": r"\bford\b|mustang|\bchevy\b|chevrolet|\bcorvette\b|\bgmc\b|\bbuick\b|\bdodge\b|\bchrysler\b|\bjeep\b|\bram\b truck|\bf-?150\b",
    "Jaguar/LR": r"jaguar|range rover|land rover|\bdefender\b|\bi-?pace\b",
    "Acura/Infiniti/Lincoln": r"\bacura|infiniti|lincoln|\bmdx\b|\btlx\b|\brdx\b",
    "Mazda/Subaru": r"\bmazda|subaru",
    "Alfa/Maserati/Ferrari": r"alfa romeo|\bgiulia\b|maserati|ferrari|lamborghini|bentley|rolls|aston martin|mclaren",
    "Chinese/Asian": r"\bxpeng\b|\bnio\b|\bbyd\b|\bli auto\b|zeekr|xiaomi|huawei|\baito\b|\bgeely\b|\blynk\b|\bsamsung\b",
    "Generic": r"competit(?!ion package|ion model|ion trim)|other brands?|other manufacturer|other makes?|other (?:luxury |premium |german |electric |ev )?(?:cars|vehicles|evs|automakers|car makers|carmakers)|previous (?:car|vehicle)|old (?:car|vehicle)|prior (?:car|vehicle)|last (?:car|vehicle)|my (?:former|previous|last|old|prior|other) |compared to|compared with|comparison|switched from|coming from|came from|traded in|trade[- ]in|than my|unlike (?:my|other|the)|cross[- ]?shop|test drove|test-drove|leased a|other ev|than (?:any )?other",
}

df = pd.read_excel(XLSX, sheet_name="Feedback_Explorer", dtype=str)
n_rows = len(df)
labels = (
    df.groupby("ID")
    .apply(lambda g: sorted(set(
        f"{(a or '').strip()} | {(b or '').strip()} | {(c or '').strip()}"
        for a, b, c in zip(g["Feedback Type"].fillna(""), g["Vfc level2 Name"].fillna(""), g["Vfc level3 Name"].fillna(""))
    )))
    .to_dict()
)
u = df.drop_duplicates("ID").copy()
txt = u["Customer Feedback"].fillna("").str.lower()

hits = {}
per_pat = Counter()
for name, pat in PATTERNS.items():
    m = txt.str.contains(pat, regex=True, flags=re.I)
    per_pat[name] = int(m.sum())
    for i in u.index[m]:
        hits.setdefault(i, []).append(name)

print(f"rows={n_rows} unique={len(u)} candidates={len(hits)}")
for k, v in per_pat.items():
    print(f"  {k:24s} {v}")

with open(OUT, "w") as f:
    for i in sorted(hits, key=lambda i: u.at[i, "ID"]):
        r = u.loc[i]
        f.write(json.dumps({
            "ID": r["ID"], "src": r["Source"], "cty": r["Country"], "eng": r["Engine Type"],
            "pats": hits[i], "labels": labels.get(r["ID"], []), "text": r["Customer Feedback"],
        }, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

133	            except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
134	                rejected.append((agent, i, f"invalid JSON: {e}"))
135	                continue
136	            err, warn = check(rec)
137	            rid = rec.get("record_id")
138	            if rid in seen:
139	                err.append(f"duplicate record_id {rid}")
140	            seen.add(rid)
141	            warnings += [(agent, i, w) for w in warn]
142	            if err:
143	                rejected.append((agent, i, "; ".join(err)))
144	                continue
145	            rec["agent"] = agent
146	            valid.append(rec)
147	
148	    with (ROOT / "findings.jsonl").open("w") as f:
149	        for rec in valid:
150	            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
151	
152	    # Feedback mix per market x vehicle x theme
153	    groups = defaultdict(lambda: {"counts": Counter(), "reviews": set(), "tiers": Counter()})
154	    for rec in valid:
155	        if rec["kind"] != "feedback":
156	            continue
157	        g = groups[(rec["market"], vehicle(rec), rec["theme"])]
158	        g["counts"][rec["feedback_type"]] += 1
159	        g["reviews"].add(rec["review_ref"])
160	        g["tiers"][rec["evidence_tier"]] += 1
161	    rows = [
162	        {"market": m, "vehicle": v, "theme": t, "basis": "web records (A=%d, B=%d)" % (g["tiers"]["A"], g["tiers"]["B"]),
163	         "n_reviews": len(g["reviews"]), "counts": g["counts"]}
164	        for (m, v, t), g in groups.items()
165	    ] + bmw_rows()
166	    types = ["Likes", "Wants", "Difficult to Use", "Defect"]
167	    with (ROOT / "theme_comparison.csv").open("w", newline="") as f:
168	        w = csv.writer(f)
169	        w.writerow(["market", "theme", "vehicle", "basis", "n_reviews", "n_statements"]
170	                   + [f"share_{t.lower().replace(' ', '_')}" for t in types] + ["share_negative"])
171	        for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["market"], r["theme"], r["vehicle"])):
172	            n = sum(r["counts"][t] for t in types)
173	            if not n:
174	                continue
175	            shares = [round(r["counts"][t] / n, 2) for t in types]
176	            neg = round((r["counts"]["Difficult to Use"] + r["counts"]["Defect"]) / n, 2)
177	            w.writerow([r["market"], r["theme"], r["vehicle"], r["basis"], r["n_reviews"], n] + shares + [neg])
178	
179	    # Equipment matrix
180	    eq = defaultdict(dict)
181	    for rec in valid:
182	        if rec["kind"] == "equipment":
183	            cell = rec["availability"] + (f": {rec['value']}" if rec.get("value") else "")
184	            key = (rec["market"], rec["feature"])
185	            veh = vehicle(rec)
186	            eq[key][veh] = (eq[key][veh] + " | " + cell) if veh in eq[key] else cell
187	    vehicles = sorted({v for cells in eq.values() for v in cells})
188	    with (ROOT / "equipment_matrix.csv").open("w", newline="") as f:
189	        w = csv.writer(f)
190	        w.writerow(["market", "feature"] + vehicles)
191	        for (m, feat) in sorted(eq):
192	            w.writerow([m, feat] + [eq[(m, feat)].get(v, "") for v in vehicles])
193	
194	    # Report
195	    kinds = Counter((r["agent"], r["kind"]) for r in valid)
196	    lines = ["# Validation report", "", f"Valid records: {len(valid)} · rejected: {len(rejected)} · warnings: {len(warnings)}", "",
197	             "| agent | kind | records |", "| --- | --- | ---: |"]
198	    lines += [f"| {a} | {k} | {n} |" for (a, k), n in sorted(kinds.items())]
199	    if rejected:
200	        lines += ["", "## Rejected", ""] + [f"- `{a}` line {i}: {e}" for a, i, e in rejected]
201	    if warnings:
202	        lines += ["", "## Warnings", ""] + [f"- `{a}` line {i}: {w}" for a, i, w in warnings]
203	    (ROOT / "validation.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
204	    print("\n".join(lines[:4 + len(kinds) + 2]))
205	
206	
207	if __name__ == "__main__":

input.content:
"""Build competitors/raw/bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl + .log.md from manual decisions (labels only, no text)."""
import json
import os
import sys
import warnings
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

import pandas as pd

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

SCRATCH = sys.argv[1]
REPO = sys.argv[2]
XLSX = os.path.join(REPO, "data", "G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx")
OUT_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, "competitors", "raw")
OUT_JSONL = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl")
OUT_LOG = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "bmw_g60_mentions.log.md")

ns = {}
exec(open(os.path.join(SCRATCH, "decisions.py")).read(), ns)
R, OWNED, UNKNOWN_PREV = ns["R"], ns["OWNED"], ns["UNKNOWN_PREV"]
SUPERL = ns.get("GENERIC_SUPERLATIVE_DROPPED", set())

themes = json.load(open(os.path.join(REPO, "competitors", "themes.json")))
THEME_IDS = {t["id"] for t in themes["themes"]}
FT = set(themes["feedback_types"])
REL = ["competitor_advantage", "bmw_advantage", "parity", "cross_shopped", "previous_car", "mention_only"]
ENGINE = {"ICE": "ICE", "PHEV": "PHEV", "BEVE": "BEV"}

df = pd.read_excel(XLSX, sheet_name="Feedback_Explorer", dtype=str)
u = df.drop_duplicates("ID").set_index("ID")
n_unique = len(u)

# ---------- validation
errors = []
seen = set()
by_id_brand = defaultdict(set)
for rec in R:
    i, brand, model, rel, theme, ft, aspect = rec
    if i not in u.index:
        errors.append(f"unknown id {i}")
    if rel not in REL:
        errors.append(f"{i} relation {rel}")
    if theme not in THEME_IDS:
        errors.append(f"{i} theme {theme}")
    if ft not in FT:
        errors.append(f"{i} feedback_type {ft}")
    if not aspect or len(aspect.split()) > 8:
        errors.append(f"{i} aspect length {aspect!r}")
    if model is not None and (not isinstance(model, str) or "network" in model.lower()):
        errors.append(f"{i} model {model!r}")
    key = (i, brand, aspect)
    if key in seen:
        errors.append(f"duplicate {key}")
    seen.add(key)
    by_id_brand[(i, brand)].add(rel)
for (i, brand), rels in by_id_brand.items():
    if "previous_car" in rels and len(rels) > 1:
        errors.append(f"{i} {brand}: previous_car next to other relations {rels}")
recorded_ids = {r[0] for r in R}
overlap = recorded_ids & UNKNOWN_PREV
if overlap:
    errors.append(f"ids both recorded and unknown-prev: {overlap}")
if errors:
    print("VALIDATION ERRORS:")
    print("\n".join(errors))
    sys.exit(1)

# ---------- records
order = {r: k for k, r in enumerate(REL)}
R_sorted = sorted(R, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1], order[r[3]], r[6]))
records = []
for k, (i, brand, model, rel, theme, ft, aspect) in enumerate(R_sorted, 1):
    row = u.loc[i]
    records.append({
        "record_id": f"bmw_g60_mentions-M{k:04d}",
        "kind": "bmw_mention",
        "bmw_feedback_id": i,
        "source": str(row["Source"]).replace("Source ", "").strip(),
        "country": row["Country"],
        "engine_type": ENGINE.get(row["Engine Type"], row["Engine Type"]),
        "competitor_brand": brand,
        "competitor_model": model,
        "relation": rel,
        "theme": theme,
        "feedback_type": ft,
        "aspect": aspect,
    })
os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
with open(OUT_JSONL, "w") as f:
    for r in records:
        f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

rec_df = pd.DataFrame(records)
assert not set(rec_df.columns) - {"record_id", "kind", "bmw_feedback_id", "source", "country", "engine_type",
                                   "competitor_brand", "competitor_model", "relation", "theme", "feedback_type", "aspect"}

# ---------- prefilter stats
def load(name):
    p = os.path.join(SCRATCH, name)
    return [json.loads(l) for l in open(p)] if os.path.exists(p) else []

v1, v2, v3 = load("g60_candidates_v1.jsonl"), load("g60_candidates_v2.jsonl"), load("g60_candidates.jsonl")
reviewed = {r["ID"] for r in v1} | {r["ID"] for r in v2} | {r["ID"] for r in v3}
not_reviewed_confirmed = recorded_ids - reviewed
pat_hits, pat_conf = Counter(), Counter()
for r in v3:
    for p in r["pats"]:
        pat_hits[p] += 1
        if r["ID"] in recorded_ids:
            pat_conf[p] += 1
brand_only = [r for r in v3 if any(p not in ("Generic", "Generic rivals", "Extra v3") for p in r["pats"])]
generic_only = [r for r in v3 if all(p in ("Generic", "Generic rivals", "Extra v3") for p in r["pats"])]


def md_table(headers, rows, align=None):
    align = align or ["---"] + ["---:"] * (len(headers) - 1)
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "| " + " | ".join(align) + " |"]
    out += ["| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return out


def crosstab(col, values=REL, sort_by_ids=True):
    rows = []
    groups = rec_df.groupby(col)
    for key, g in groups:
        ids = g["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
        cells = []
        for v in values:
            gv = g[g["relation"] == v]
            cells.append(f"{gv['bmw_feedback_id'].nunique()} / {len(gv)}" if len(gv) else "–")
        rows.append([key, ids, len(g)] + cells)
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[1], -r[2], str(r[0])))
    return rows


L = []
L += ["# BMW G60 verbatims that mention competitors (log)", "",
      "Agent: `bmw_g60_mentions` · input: `data/G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` (sheet `Feedback_Explorer`) · "
      "output: `bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl` (`kind: \"bmw_mention\"`, labels only, no verbatim text).", "",
      "Cells written as **`a / b`** mean `a` unique BMW feedback IDs / `b` records. Count IDs, not records "
      "(one verbatim can carry several competitors or aspects).", ""]

L += ["## Method", "",
      f"1. Deduplicated {len(df):,} classification rows to **{n_unique:,} unique feedback IDs** (all rows of one ID have the same text).",
      "2. Ran a broad regex prefilter in three passes:",
      "   - Brand and model names, plus common misspellings.",
      "   - Model codes (e.g. E 350, C-200) and KR/JP market names (Grandeur, Sonata, K8 …).",
      "   - Generic comparison phrases (\"compared to\", \"previous car\", \"other brands\", \"rivals\", \"switched from\", \"cross-shop\" …).",
      "   - Fixes made during the review: an `audi` pattern without a word boundary matched \"audio\", so it was corrected; `g wagon` and hyphenated model codes were added.",
      f"3. Every candidate text was read by hand ({len(reviewed)} unique IDs across the passes). Discarded:",
      "   - golf bags/clubs, Samsung phones, \"electronic\" (matched e-tron), Electrify America \"supercharger\", loaner/rental cars;",
      "   - comparisons with BMW's own models (G30, X5, 540i, iX, i4 …);",
      "   - the BMW M/Competition trims;",
      "   - generic \"best car I've ever had\" superlatives;",
      "   - generic wishes for \"full self-driving\" that name no brand;",
      "   - Apple products.",
      "4. Coding rules:",
      "   - One record per (feedback ID, competitor, aspect).",
      "   - Directional records (`competitor_advantage` / `bmw_advantage` / `parity`) are written per compared aspect.",
      "   - `cross_shopped` is added when the customer says they considered or test drove the competitor. Its aspect is \"Purchase consideration\" when the compared aspect already has a directional record.",
      "   - `previous_car` is used **only** when the customer says they came from the brand and makes no directional comparison.",
      "   - Prior or concurrent ownership is tracked separately (table below), so it does not inflate `previous_car`.",
      "   - Source B: only competitors raised by the customer count. Mentions made only by the call-centre writer were dropped.",
      "5. Generic statements (`competitor_brand: \"generic\"`) are kept only when they make a specific comparison on an aspect.",
      "   - Examples: \"sound system weak compared to rivals\", \"better put together than other brands\", \"less sensitive than others I have used\".",
      "   - Brand groups that the customer names are kept as such: `Japanese brands`, `Korean brands`, `German brands`.",
      "   - Statements that the customer is considering other brands, with no brand named, are kept as `generic` + `mention_only` + aspect \"Considering other brands\". Filter them out if you do not need them.",
      "6. `theme` is the compared aspect, judged by hand. The BMW VFC level2 → theme mapping was used only as a hint.",
      "7. `feedback_type` describes the BMW side of that aspect (Likes / Wants / Difficult to Use / Defect).",
      "8. `engine_type` uses BEV for BMW's `BEVE`, consistent with `tools/bmw_baseline.py`.",
      "9. Tesla Supercharger and NACS-adapter mentions are coded as `Tesla` with `competitor_model: null`. The network appears only in the aspect label.", ""]

L += ["## Prefilter hits vs confirmed", ""]
L += md_table(["", "unique feedback IDs"], [
    ["unique feedbacks scanned", n_unique],
    ["prefilter pass 1 (initial)", len({r['ID'] for r in v1})],
    ["prefilter pass 2 (fixed Audi boundary, + misspellings, model codes, KR/JP names, rivals)", len({r['ID'] for r in v2})],
    ["prefilter final pass (+ hyphenated codes, G-Wagon, Avant/allroad, extra KR names, EU brands, 'another brand')", len({r['ID'] for r in v3})],
    ["  of which hit a brand/model pattern", len(brand_only)],
    ["  of which hit only generic comparison phrases", len(generic_only)],
    ["union of all candidates read manually", len(reviewed)],
    ["**confirmed (≥1 record)**", f"**{len(recorded_ids)}**"],
    ["  confirmed with a named brand/group (not `generic`)", rec_df[rec_df.competitor_brand != 'generic']['bmw_feedback_id'].nunique()],
    ["  confirmed with `generic` only", len(recorded_ids - set(rec_df[rec_df.competitor_brand != 'generic']['bmw_feedback_id']))],
    ["comparison with a previous/other vehicle of unknown brand (not recorded)", len(UNKNOWN_PREV)],
    ["generic superlatives dropped (\"better than any other car\")", len(SUPERL)],
    ["other discards (false positives, BMW-own comparisons, no comparison)", len(reviewed) - len(recorded_ids) - len(UNKNOWN_PREV) - len(SUPERL)],
    ["**records written**", f"**{len(records)}**"],
], ["---", "---:"])
if not_reviewed_confirmed:
    L += ["", f"Note: {len(not_reviewed_confirmed)} confirmed IDs were outside the candidate files: {sorted(not_reviewed_confirmed)}"]
L += ["", "Per prefilter pattern group (final pass; an ID can hit several groups):", ""]
L += md_table(["pattern group", "hits (IDs)", "confirmed (IDs)", "precision"],
              [[p, pat_hits[p], pat_conf[p], f"{pat_conf[p] / pat_hits[p]:.0%}"] for p in sorted(pat_hits, key=lambda p: -pat_hits[p])])
L += [""]

L += ["## Competitor brand × relation", "", "`a / b` = unique IDs / records.", ""]
L += md_table(["competitor_brand", "IDs", "records"] + REL, crosstab("competitor_brand"))
L += [""]

# net view per brand
L += ["### Net view per brand (directional records only)", ""]
rows = []
for b, g in rec_df.groupby("competitor_brand"):
    ca = g[g.relation == "competitor_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    ba = g[g.relation == "bmw_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    pa = g[g.relation == "parity"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    if ca + ba + pa:
        rows.append([b, ca, ba, pa, ba - ca])
rows.sort(key=lambda r: -(r[1] + r[2] + r[3]))
L += md_table(["competitor_brand", "IDs: competitor better", "IDs: BMW better", "IDs: parity", "net (BMW − competitor)"], rows)
L += [""]

L += ["### Competitor models named", ""]
mm = rec_df[rec_df.competitor_model.notna()].groupby(["competitor_brand", "competitor_model"])["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
L += md_table(["brand", "model", "IDs"], [[b, m, n] for (b, m), n in mm.items()], ["---", "---", "---:"])
L += [""]

L += ["### Customer owns or owned the competitor (previous car or second car in the household)", "",
      "Tracked apart from `relation`, so a former Tesla owner who compares charging is counted here **and** under `competitor_advantage`.", ""]
oc = Counter(b for _, b in OWNED)
L += md_table(["competitor_brand", "IDs"], [[b, n] for b, n in oc.most_common()], ["---", "---:"])
L += [f"", f"Total: {len({i for i, _ in OWNED})} unique feedback IDs with a stated competitor ownership.", ""]

L += ["## Theme × relation (where competitors are seen as better vs worse)", "", "`a / b` = unique IDs / records.", ""]
L += md_table(["theme", "IDs", "records"] + REL, crosstab("theme"))
L += [""]
rows = []
for t, g in rec_df.groupby("theme"):
    ca = g[g.relation == "competitor_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    ba = g[g.relation == "bmw_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    if ca + ba:
        rows.append([t, ca, ba, ba - ca, "BMW ahead" if ba > ca else ("competitors ahead" if ca > ba else "even")])
rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[3])
L += ["### Net per theme (unique IDs, competitor_advantage vs bmw_advantage)", ""]
L += md_table(["theme", "competitor better", "BMW better", "net", "reading"], rows, ["---", "---:", "---:", "---:", "---"])
L += [""]

# per source / country / engine
src_tot = u["Source"].str.replace("Source ", "").value_counts()
L += ["## Per source (A–D)", "", "Share = confirmed IDs / all unique G60 feedbacks of that source.", ""]
rows = []
for s, g in rec_df.groupby("source"):
    ids = g["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    named = g[g.competitor_brand != "generic"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    rows.append([s, src_tot.get(s, 0), ids, f"{ids / src_tot.get(s, 1):.1%}", named, len(g),
                 g[g.relation == "competitor_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique(),
                 g[g.relation == "bmw_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()])
L += md_table(["source", "G60 feedbacks", "confirmed IDs", "share", "IDs with named brand", "records",
               "IDs competitor better", "IDs BMW better"], sorted(rows), ["---"] + ["---:"] * 7)
L += [""]

cty_tot = u["Country"].value_counts()
L += ["## Per country", ""]
rows = []
for c, g in rec_df.groupby("country"):
    ids = g["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    top = g[g.competitor_brand != "generic"].groupby("competitor_brand")["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
    rows.append([c, cty_tot.get(c, 0), ids, f"{ids / cty_tot.get(c, 1):.1%}", len(g),
                 ", ".join(f"{b} {n}" for b, n in top.head(4).items()) or "–"])
rows.sort(key=lambda r: -r[2])
L += md_table(["country", "G60 feedbacks", "confirmed IDs", "share", "records", "top named brands (IDs)"],
              rows, ["---", "---:", "---:", "---:", "---:", "---"])
L += [""]

eng_tot = u["Engine Type"].map(ENGINE).value_counts()
L += ["## Per engine type", ""]
rows = []
for e, g in rec_df.groupby("engine_type"):
    ids = g["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    top = g[g.competitor_brand != "generic"].groupby("competitor_brand")["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
    rows.append([e, eng_tot.get(e, 0), ids, f"{ids / eng_tot.get(e, 1):.1%}", len(g),
                 g[g.relation == "competitor_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique(),
                 g[g.relation == "bmw_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique(),
                 ", ".join(f"{b} {n}" for b, n in top.head(4).items())])
L += md_table(["engine_type", "G60 feedbacks", "confirmed IDs", "share", "records", "IDs competitor better",
               "IDs BMW better", "top named brands (IDs)"], rows, ["---"] + ["---:"] * 6 + ["---"])
L += [""]


def top_aspects(rel, n=15):
    g = rec_df[rec_df.relation == rel]
    agg = g.groupby(["aspect", "theme"]).agg(ids=("bmw_feedback_id", "nunique"), records=("record_id", "count"),
                                             brands=("competitor_brand", lambda s: ", ".join(f"{b} {c}" for b, c in Counter(s).most_common(4))))
    agg = agg.sort_values(["ids", "records"], ascending=False).head(n)
    return [[a, t, r.ids, r.records, r.brands] for (a, t), r in agg.iterrows()]


L += ["## Top aspects where competitors are seen as better (`competitor_advantage`)", ""]
L += md_table(["aspect", "theme", "IDs", "records", "brands (records)"], top_aspects("competitor_advantage", 20),
              ["---", "---", "---:", "---:", "---"])
L += ["", "## Top aspects where BMW is seen as better (`bmw_advantage`)", ""]
L += md_table(["aspect", "theme", "IDs", "records", "brands (records)"], top_aspects("bmw_advantage", 20),
              ["---", "---", "---:", "---:", "---"])
L += ["", "## Parity, cross-shopping, previous car, mention only", ""]
for rel in ("parity", "cross_shopped", "previous_car", "mention_only"):
    L += [f"**{rel}**", ""]
    L += md_table(["aspect", "theme", "IDs", "records", "brands (records)"], top_aspects(rel, 12),
                  ["---", "---", "---:", "---:", "---"])

"""Build competitors/raw/bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl + .log.md from manual decisions (labels only, no text)."""
import json
import os
import sys
import warnings
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

import pandas as pd

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

SCRATCH = sys.argv[1]
REPO = sys.argv[2]
XLSX = os.path.join(REPO, "data", "G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx")
OUT_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, "competitors", "raw")
OUT_JSONL = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl")
OUT_LOG = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "bmw_g60_mentions.log.md")

ns = {}
exec(open(os.path.join(SCRATCH, "decisions.py")).read(), ns)
R, OWNED, UNKNOWN_PREV = ns["R"], ns["OWNED"], ns["UNKNOWN_PREV"]
SUPERL = ns.get("GENERIC_SUPERLATIVE_DROPPED", set())

themes = json.load(open(os.path.join(REPO, "competitors", "themes.json")))
THEME_IDS = {t["id"] for t in themes["themes"]}
FT = set(themes["feedback_types"])
REL = ["competitor_advantage", "bmw_advantage", "parity", "cross_shopped", "previous_car", "mention_only"]
ENGINE = {"ICE": "ICE", "PHEV": "PHEV", "BEVE": "BEV"}

df = pd.read_excel(XLSX, sheet_name="Feedback_Explorer", dtype=str)
u = df.drop_duplicates("ID").set_index("ID")
n_unique = len(u)

# ---------- validation
errors = []
seen = set()
by_id_brand = defaultdict(set)
for rec in R:
    i, brand, model, rel, theme, ft, aspect = rec
    if i not in u.index:
        errors.append(f"unknown id {i}")
    if rel not in REL:
        errors.append(f"{i} relation {rel}")
    if theme not in THEME_IDS:
        errors.append(f"{i} theme {theme}")
    if ft not in FT:
        errors.append(f"{i} feedback_type {ft}")
    if not aspect or len(aspect.split()) > 8:
        errors.append(f"{i} aspect length {aspect!r}")
    if model is not None and (not isinstance(model, str) or "network" in model.lower()):
        errors.append(f"{i} model {model!r}")
    key = (i, brand, aspect)
    if key in seen:
        errors.append(f"duplicate {key}")
    seen.add(key)
    by_id_brand[(i, brand)].add(rel)
for (i, brand), rels in by_id_brand.items():
    if "previous_car" in rels and len(rels) > 1:
        errors.append(f"{i} {brand}: previous_car next to other relations {rels}")
recorded_ids = {r[0] for r in R}
overlap = recorded_ids & UNKNOWN_PREV
if overlap:
    errors.append(f"ids both recorded and unknown-prev: {overlap}")
if errors:
    print("VALIDATION ERRORS:")
    print("\n".join(errors))
    sys.exit(1)

# ---------- records
order = {r: k for k, r in enumerate(REL)}
R_sorted = sorted(R, key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1], order[r[3]], r[6]))
records = []
for k, (i, brand, model, rel, theme, ft, aspect) in enumerate(R_sorted, 1):
    row = u.loc[i]
    records.append({
        "record_id": f"bmw_g60_mentions-M{k:04d}",
        "kind": "bmw_mention",
        "bmw_feedback_id": i,
        "source": str(row["Source"]).replace("Source ", "").strip(),
        "country": row["Country"],
        "engine_type": ENGINE.get(row["Engine Type"], row["Engine Type"]),
        "competitor_brand": brand,
        "competitor_model": model,
        "relation": rel,
        "theme": theme,
        "feedback_type": ft,
        "aspect": aspect,
    })
os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
with open(OUT_JSONL, "w") as f:
    for r in records:
        f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

rec_df = pd.DataFrame(records)
assert not set(rec_df.columns) - {"record_id", "kind", "bmw_feedback_id", "source", "country", "engine_type",
                                   "competitor_brand", "competitor_model", "relation", "theme", "feedback_type", "aspect"}

# ---------- prefilter stats
def load(name):
    p = os.path.join(SCRATCH, name)
    return [json.loads(l) for l in open(p)] if os.path.exists(p) else []

v1, v2, v3 = load("g60_candidates_v1.jsonl"), load("g60_candidates_v2.jsonl"), load("g60_candidates.jsonl")
reviewed = {r["ID"] for r in v1} | {r["ID"] for r in v2} | {r["ID"] for r in v3}
not_reviewed_confirmed = recorded_ids - reviewed
pat_hits, pat_conf = Counter(), Counter()
for r in v3:
    for p in r["pats"]:
        pat_hits[p] += 1
        if r["ID"] in recorded_ids:
            pat_conf[p] += 1
brand_only = [r for r in v3 if any(p not in ("Generic", "Generic rivals", "Extra v3") for p in r["pats"])]
generic_only = [r for r in v3 if all(p in ("Generic", "Generic rivals", "Extra v3") for p in r["pats"])]


def md_table(headers, rows, align=None):
    align = align or ["---"] + ["---:"] * (len(headers) - 1)
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "| " + " | ".join(align) + " |"]
    out += ["| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return out


def crosstab(col, values=REL, sort_by_ids=True):
    rows = []
    groups = rec_df.groupby(col)
    for key, g in groups:
        ids = g["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
        cells = []
        for v in values:
            gv = g[g["relation"] == v]
            cells.append(f"{gv['bmw_feedback_id'].nunique()} / {len(gv)}" if len(gv) else "–")
        rows.append([key, ids, len(g)] + cells)
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[1], -r[2], str(r[0])))
    return rows

L += ["# BMW G60 verbatims that mention competitors (log)", "",
      "Agent: `bmw_g60_mentions` · input: `data/G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` (sheet `Feedback_Explorer`) · "

      "(one verbatim can carry several competitors or aspects).", ""]

      f"1. Deduplicated {len(df):,} classification rows to **{n_unique:,} unique feedback IDs** (all rows of one ID have the same text).",
      "2. Ran a broad regex prefilter in three passes:",
      "   - Brand and model names, plus common misspellings.",
      "   - Model codes (e.g. E 350, C-200) and KR/JP market names (Grandeur, Sonata, K8 …).",
      "   - Generic comparison phrases (\"compared to\", \"previous car\", \"other brands\", \"rivals\", \"switched from\", \"cross-shop\" …).",
      "   - Fixes made during the review: an `audi` pattern without a word boundary matched \"audio\", so it was corrected; `g wagon` and hyphenated model codes were added.",
      f"3. Every candidate text was read by hand ({len(reviewed)} unique IDs across the passes). Discarded:",
      "   - golf bags/clubs, Samsung phones, \"electronic\" (matched e-tron), Electrify America \"supercharger\", loaner/rental cars;",
      "   - comparisons with BMW's own models (G30, X5, 540i, iX, i4 …);",

      "   - generic \"best car I've ever had\" superlatives;",
      "   - generic wishes for \"full self-driving\" that name no brand;",
      "   - Apple products.",
      "4. Coding rules:",
      "   - One record per (feedback ID, competitor, aspect).",
      "   - Directional records (`competitor_advantage` / `bmw_advantage` / `parity`) are written per compared aspect.",
      "   - `cross_shopped` is added when the customer says they considered or test drove the competitor. Its aspect is \"Purchase consideration\" when the compared aspect already has a directional record.",
      "   - `previous_car` is used **only** when the customer says they came from the brand and makes no directional comparison.",
      "   - Prior or concurrent ownership is tracked separately (table below), so it does not inflate `previous_car`.",
      "   - Source B: only competitors raised by the customer count. Mentions made only by the call-centre writer were dropped.",
      "5. Generic statements (`competitor_brand: \"generic\"`) are kept only when they make a specific comparison on an aspect.",

      "   - Brand groups that the customer names are kept as such: `Japanese brands`, `Korean brands`, `German brands`.",

      "8. `engine_type` uses BEV for BMW's `BEVE`, consistent with `tools/bmw_baseline.py`.",

    ["  of which hit a brand/model pattern", len(brand_only)],
    ["  of which hit only generic comparison phrases", len(generic_only)],
    ["union of all candidates read manually", len(reviewed)],
    ["**confirmed (≥1 record)**", f"**{len(recorded_ids)}**"],
    ["  confirmed with a named brand/group (not `generic`)", rec_df[rec_df.competitor_brand != 'generic']['bmw_feedback_id'].nunique()],
    ["  confirmed with `generic` only", len(recorded_ids - set(rec_df[rec_df.competitor_brand != 'generic']['bmw_feedback_id']))],
    ["comparison with a previous/other vehicle of unknown brand (not recorded)", len(UNKNOWN_PREV)],
    ["generic superlatives dropped (\"better than any other car\")", len(SUPERL)],
    ["other discards (false positives, BMW-own comparisons, no comparison)", len(reviewed) - len(recorded_ids) - len(UNKNOWN_PREV) - len(SUPERL)],
    ["**records written**", f"**{len(records)}**"],
], ["---", "---:"])
if not_reviewed_confirmed:
    L += ["", f"Note: {len(not_reviewed_confirmed)} confirmed IDs were outside the candidate files: {sorted(not_reviewed_confirmed)}"]
L += ["", "Per prefilter pattern group (final pass; an ID can hit several groups):", ""]
L += md_table(["pattern group", "hits (IDs)", "confirmed (IDs)", "precision"],
              [[p, pat_hits[p], pat_conf[p], f"{pat_conf[p] / pat_hits[p]:.0%}"] for p in sorted(pat_hits, key=lambda p: -pat_hits[p])])

L += [""]

rows = []
for b, g in rec_df.groupby("competitor_brand"):
    ca = g[g.relation == "competitor_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()
    ba = g[g.relation == "bmw_advantage"]["bmw_feedback_id"].nunique()

18	   - the BMW M/Competition trims;
19	   - generic "best car I've ever had" superlatives;
20	   - generic wishes for "full self-driving" that name no brand;
21	   - Apple products.
22	4. Coding rules:
23	   - One record per (feedback ID, competitor, aspect).
24	   - Directional records (`competitor_advantage` / `bmw_advantage` / `parity`) are written per compared aspect.
25	   - `cross_shopped` is added when the customer says they considered or test drove the competitor. Its aspect is "Purchase consideration" when the compared aspect already has a directional record.
26	   - `previous_car` is used **only** when the customer says they came from the brand and makes no directional comparison.
27	   - Prior or concurrent ownership is tracked separately (table below), so it does not inflate `previous_car`.
28	   - Source B: only competitors raised by the customer count. Mentions made only by the call-centre writer were dropped.
29	5. Generic statements (`competitor_brand: "generic"`) are kept only when they make a specific comparison on an aspect.
30	   - Examples: "sound system weak compared to rivals", "better put together than other brands", "less sensitive than others I have used".
31	   - Brand groups that the customer names are kept as such: `Japanese brands`, `Korean brands`, `German brands`.
32	   - Statements that the customer is considering other brands, with no brand named, are kept as `generic` + `mention_only` + aspect "Considering other brands". Filter them out if you do not need them.
33	6. `theme` is the compared aspect, judged by hand. The BMW VFC level2 → theme mapping was used only as a hint.
34	7. `feedback_type` describes the BMW side of that aspect (Likes / Wants / Difficult to Use / Defect).
35	8. `engine_type` uses BEV for BMW's `BEVE`, consistent with `tools/bmw_baseline.py`.
36	9. Tesla Supercharger and NACS-adapter mentions are coded as `Tesla` with `competitor_model: null`. The network appears only in the aspect label.

451	- **Source effects.**
452	  - Source B is a third-person call-centre paraphrase and only keeps comparisons the customer raised.
453	  - Sources C and D are structured survey answers and contain few comparisons.
454	  - Source A is the closest match to competitor owner reviews.
455	- **BEV selection.** i5 (BEV) owners are over-represented among competitor mentions, mostly Tesla converts. EV charging and range topics therefore dominate `competitor_advantage`.
456	- **Prior ownership is not loyalty.** Many confirmed IDs come from conquest customers (ex-Tesla, ex-Audi, ex-Mercedes, ex-Lexus) who explain why they switched. That biases the record set toward `bmw_advantage`.
457	- **Judgement calls.**
458	  - Relation, theme and aspect were coded by hand from one reading. Borderline cases were coded conservatively, e.g. a Genesis ride that was only called "different" became `previous_car`, not `competitor_advantage`.
459	  - Generic "other cars" superlatives were dropped.
460	  - 35 comparisons with a previous vehicle of unknown brand were not recorded, because many are likely earlier BMWs.
461	- **Prefilter recall.** The regex is broad and was run in three passes with misspelling variants. Comparisons that neither name a brand nor use a comparison phrase can still be missed.
462	- **Confidentiality.** No verbatim text or paraphrase is stored, only IDs and short labels.

input.message:
I found **191 of the 4,000 G60 feedback IDs (4.8%)** that name or clearly compare against a competitor, and wrote them as **255 `bmw_mention` records**. Customers see BMW ahead on driving and build quality, and competitors ahead on charging, driver assistance, infotainment, connectivity and space.

Every record passes `merge.check()` from `competitors/tools/merge.py`. I called the function directly, so `main()` did not run and no merged files were written. A 5-word overlap check against all verbatims found no matches in either output file, so no BMW text leaked. No other repo files were changed and no git was run.

**How the candidates were found.** A regex prefilter ran in three passes and I read all 448 candidate texts by hand. Your existing prefilter matched "audio" as Audi; I fixed that and added misspellings, model codes such as "C-200", "G wagon", and KR/JP names like Grandeur and Sonata. Of the candidates, 191 were confirmed, 35 compared with a previous car of unknown brand (not recorded, many are likely earlier BMWs), and 4 generic "better than any other car" statements were dropped. The rest were false positives (golf bags, Samsung phones, loaners) or comparisons with BMW's own models.

**Top brands (unique IDs):**

| Brand | IDs |
| --- | ---: |
| Tesla | 66 |
| Mercedes-Benz | 32 (8 name the E-Class) |
| generic ("rivals", "other brands") | 32 |
| Audi | 23 |
| Lexus | 9 |
| Hyundai | 7 |
| Cadillac | 6 |
| Volvo, Toyota, Porsche | 4 each |

The net per brand is negative for Tesla: 33 IDs competitor better vs 27 BMW better. Mercedes (14 vs 15) and Audi (8 vs 10) come out about even.

**Top 5 competitor-advantage aspects (IDs):**
1. Public fast-charging network: 9, all Tesla. Including the Supercharger adapter and access mentions, Tesla charging access covers **14 IDs**.
2. Electric range: 5 (Tesla 3, Mercedes EQE 1, generic 1)
3. Sound system: 4 (Audi 2, Toyota 1, generic 1)
4. Remote app features: 3 (Lincoln, Mercedes, Hyundai, Tesla)
5. Rear cross-traffic alert: 3 (Kia, generic 2)

These lists understate driver assistance and infotainment. Competitors are ahead there on 17 and 12 IDs, but the losses are spread over many 1–2-ID aspects (automated parking, sign recognition, collision warning, voice assistant, physical controls). Net by theme, competitors lead on charging/range (−16), driver assistance and parking (−14), connectivity (−7), infotainment (−7) and space (−7).

**Top BMW-advantage aspects (IDs):**
1. Handling and driving dynamics: 16 (Tesla, Mercedes, Audi, Porsche, Lucid)
2. Build quality: 11 (8 of them vs Tesla)
3. Ride comfort: 8 (Mercedes 4, Tesla 3)
4. Value for money: 6
5. A tie at 5: overall vehicle, and acceleration and power

Net by theme, BMW leads on ride and handling (+20), overall quality and ownership (+14), value (+6) and powertrain (+5).

**Caveats:**
- **Mostly US and EV.** 163 of the 191 IDs are US, and only 6 come from the EU. i5 (BEV) owners, many of them ex-Tesla, drive the charging and range signal.
- **Counts are small.** Most aspects have 1–5 IDs, so treat them as qualitative signals, not shares.
- **Ownership is only in the log.** 90 IDs say the customer owns or owned the competitor, but only 7 carry `relation: previous_car`. I kept that relation for cases with no better/worse comparison. Anyone looking at where switchers come from should use the ownership table in the log, not the JSONL.
- **Parity can be negative.** 7 of the 11 parity IDs mean "BMW has become more like X", for example more touch controls or a less sporty feel.
- **Switch intent is a floor.** "Considering other brands" (generic, `mention_only`) only counts statements that refer to another brand.
- **Coding choices.**
  - `engine_type` is BEV where the source data says BEVE, to match `bmw_baseline.py`; joins back to the xlsx need that mapping.
  - Tesla Supercharger mentions use `competitor_model: null`, with the network named only in the aspect label.
  - Groups the customer names are kept as brands: Japanese, Korean and German brands.
  - Relation, theme and aspect are my own judgement from one reading each.

Files are in `/Users/luisdehlwes/Documents/00_Events/EHL Finale/worktrees/luis-competitors/competitors/raw/`:
- bmw_g60_mentions.jsonl
- bmw_g60_mentions.log.md

The scripts to rebuild them (`decisions.py`, `build_mentions.py`, `verify_outputs.py`, `g60_prefilter.py`) are in the scratchpad folder: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-luisdehlwes-Documents-00-Events-EHL-Finale/17a2c20e-7947-4abe-8706-20475727794d/scratchpad/`
